paragraphs: Leicester City Council looks after more than 600 children, and it recruits its own foster carers for them as well as working with independent agencies such as those shown above, which list Leicester among the places they cover. Fostering for the city council means caring for Leicester's own children with the team that plans for them; an agency recruits, trains and supports its own carers and offers homes to councils that need them.

The need is local and pressing. During Foster Care Fortnight in May 2026 the council said it urgently needs more foster carers, because when there are not enough carers nearby children can end up living outside the city, away from the people and places they know. The Fostering Network, speaking alongside the council, said many carers are leaving while the number of children coming into care is rising. In October 2025 Leicester was one of more than 90 councils behind The Run, a short film about fostering that follows an 11-year-old boy.

You can apply if you live in Leicester, Leicestershire, Rutland or a neighbouring county. The council says applicants are usually over 25, with no upper age limit, and single people and couples are both welcome. You need a secure home with a spare room but do not need to own it, and a disability or minor health problem will not rule you out. Smoking matters: a household with a smoker cannot foster a child under five or most disabled children, and ex-smokers need to have stopped for at least 12 months. Everyone in the household is checked.

Our Leicester allowance page sets out what the city pays: a weekly amount for each child from £182 for under-fives to £267 for young people of 16 and over, plus a weekly accreditation payment per child of £50 for newly approved carers, £90 once established after a year, £250 for enhanced fostering and £440 for specialist fostering. Carers also get an extra week's allowance for a birthday and for a festival, and two extra weeks a year for holidays. The council's page does not say which year the rates are for, so check them with the team.

The council's fostering team is on 0116 454 4500 and runs informal information events. Leicestershire County Council has a separate service for the rest of the county, so see the Leicestershire page too, and the Rutland, Coventry and Northamptonshire pages if you live nearby. Talk to the council and two or three of the services above before you decide.
